source.text: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ Σαδδουκαῖοι, λέγοντες μὴ εἶναι ἀνάστασιν, καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Διδάσκαλε, Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν· Ἐάν τις ἀποθάνῃ μὴ ἔχων τέκνα, ἐπιγαμβρεύσει ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστήσει σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: On that day came to him Sadducees, saying not to be a resurrection, and they questioned him, \v 24 saying, Teacher, Moses said, If anyone should die not having children, will marry the brother of him the wife of him and will raise up offspring for the brother of him.

en.L: On that day Sadducees came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying that there is no resurrection, and they questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 24 saying, "Teacher, Moses said, 'If anyone dies having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.'
en.B: That same day some Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with a question. \v 24 "Teacher," they said, "Moses gave this rule: 'If a man dies and leaves no children, his brother is to take the widow as his wife and so give his dead brother descendants.'
en.R: That same day some Sadducees came to Jesus. The Sadducees taught that dead people do not rise to life again. They asked Jesus a question. \v 24 They said, "Teacher, Moses wrote in the law, 'If a man dies without children, his brother must marry the dead man's wife. Then their children will count as the children of the brother who died.'

es.L: Aquel día se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron saduceos, que dicen que no hay resurrección, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron, \v 24 diciendo: «Maestro, Moisés dijo: “Si alguien muere sin tener hijos, su hermano tomará por esposa a la mujer de este y levantará descendencia para su hermano”.
es.B: Ese mismo día se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron unos saduceos, que dicen que no hay resurrección, con una pregunta. \v 24 «Maestro», le dijeron, «Moisés dio esta norma: “Si un hombre muere sin dejar hijos, su hermano debe casarse con la viuda y así darle descendientes a su hermano muerto”.
es.R: Ese mismo día, unos saduceos se acercaron a Jesús. Los saduceos enseñaban que los muertos no vuelven a la vida. Le hicieron a Jesús una pregunta. \v 24 Le dijeron: «Maestro, Moisés escribió en la ley: “Si un hombre muere sin tener hijos, su hermano tiene que casarse con la viuda. Así, los hijos que tengan contarán como hijos del hermano que murió”.

fr.L: En ce jour-là, des Sadducéens s’approchèrent de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, disant qu’il n’y a pas de résurrection, et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogèrent, \v 24 disant : « Maître, Moïse a dit : “Si quelqu’un meurt sans avoir d’enfants, son frère épousera sa femme et suscitera une descendance à son frère.”
fr.B: Ce même jour, des Sadducéens, qui disent qu’il n’y a pas de résurrection, vinrent {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} poser une question. \v 24 « Maître, dirent-ils, Moïse a donné cette règle : “Si un homme meurt sans laisser d’enfants, son frère doit épouser la veuve et donner ainsi une descendance à son frère mort.”
fr.R: Le même jour, des Sadducéens sont venus voir Jésus. Les Sadducéens enseignaient que les morts ne reviennent pas à la vie. Ils ont posé une question à Jésus. \v 24 Ils ont dit : « Maître, Moïse a écrit dans la Loi : “Si un homme meurt sans enfants, son frère doit épouser la femme du mort. Alors leurs enfants seront comptés comme les enfants du frère mort.”

sw.L: Siku hiyo Masadukayo walimjia, wakisema kwamba hakuna ufufuo, nao wakamwuliza, \v 24 wakisema, "Mwalimu, Musa alisema, 'Ikiwa mtu yeyote atakufa bila kuwa na watoto, ndugu yake atamwoa mke wake na kumwinulia ndugu yake uzao.'
sw.B: Siku hiyo hiyo baadhi ya Masadukayo, wanaosema kwamba hakuna ufufuo, walimjia na swali. \v 24 Wakasema, "Mwalimu, Musa alitoa agizo hili: 'Mtu akifariki bila kuacha watoto, ndugu yake anapaswa kumwoa mjane huyo ili ampatie ndugu yake aliyekufa wazao.'
sw.R: Siku hiyo hiyo baadhi ya Masadukayo walikuja kwa Yesu. Masadukayo walifundisha kwamba wafu hawafufuki. Wakamwuliza Yesu swali. \v 24 Wakasema, "Mwalimu, Musa aliandika katika sheria, 'Mtu akifa bila kuwa na watoto, ndugu yake lazima amwoe mke wa marehemu. Kisha watoto watakaozaliwa watahesabiwa kuwa watoto wa ndugu aliyekufa.'

vi.L: Trong ngày ấy, có những người Sa-đu-sê, là những người nói rằng không có sự sống lại, đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 24 nói rằng: "Thưa Thầy, Môi-se đã nói: 'Nếu ai chết mà không có con, thì anh em của người ấy phải cưới vợ của người ấy và sinh dòng dõi cho anh em mình.'
vi.B: Cũng trong ngày ấy, có mấy người Sa-đu-sê đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ cho rằng không có sự sống lại, và họ đặt câu hỏi với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 24 Họ nói: "Thưa Thầy, Môi-se đã truyền luật này: 'Nếu một người chết mà không có con, thì anh em của người ấy phải cưới người vợ góa và sinh con để nối dõi cho người đã chết.'
vi.R: Cũng trong ngày đó, có mấy người Sa-đu-sê đến gặp Đức Giê-xu. Người Sa-đu-sê dạy rằng người chết sẽ không sống lại. Họ hỏi Đức Giê-xu một câu. \v 24 Họ nói: "Thưa Thầy, Môi-se đã viết trong luật pháp: 'Nếu một người đàn ông chết mà không có con, thì anh em của người ấy phải cưới người vợ góa. Rồi con cái họ sinh ra sẽ được kể là con của người anh em đã chết.'

ko.L: 그날에 부활이 없다고 말하는 사두개파 사람들이 그분께 다가와서 그분께 물었다. \v 24 "선생님, 모세가 말하기를, '누가 자녀 없이 죽으면, 그의 형제가 그의 아내를 맞아들여 자기 형제를 위하여 씨를 일으켜야 한다'고 하였습니다.
ko.B: 같은 날, 부활이 없다고 주장하는 사두개파 사람들이 예수께 와서 물었다. \v 24 "선생님, 모세는 '어떤 사람이 자식 없이 죽으면, 그의 형제가 그 과부와 결혼하여 죽은 형제의 대를 이을 자식을 낳아 주어야 한다'고 말했습니다.
ko.R: 그날 사두개파 사람 몇 명이 예수께 왔다. 사두개파 사람들은 죽은 사람이 다시 살아나지 않는다고 가르쳤다. 그들이 예수께 질문을 했다. \v 24 그들이 말했다. "선생님, 모세가 율법에 이렇게 썼습니다. '어떤 남자가 자식 없이 죽으면, 그의 형제가 죽은 사람의 아내와 결혼해야 한다. 그러면 그들이 낳는 자식은 죽은 형제의 자식으로 여겨진다.'

pt.L: Naquele dia, vieram até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} saduceus, dizendo que não há ressurreição, e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} interrogaram, \v 24 dizendo: "Mestre, Moisés disse: 'Se alguém morrer sem ter filhos, o irmão dele se casará com a mulher dele e suscitará descendência para o irmão.'
pt.B: Naquele mesmo dia, alguns saduceus, que dizem não haver ressurreição, vieram até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} com uma pergunta. \v 24 "Mestre", disseram eles, "Moisés deu esta regra: 'Se um homem morrer sem deixar filhos, o irmão dele deve se casar com a viúva e assim dar descendentes ao irmão que morreu.'
pt.R: Naquele mesmo dia, alguns saduceus foram falar com Jesus. Os saduceus ensinavam que os mortos não voltam a viver. Eles fizeram uma pergunta a Jesus. \v 24 Disseram: "Mestre, Moisés escreveu na Lei: 'Se um homem morrer sem ter filhos, o irmão dele tem de se casar com a viúva. Assim, os filhos que eles tiverem vão contar como filhos do irmão que morreu.'

am.L: በዚያ ቀን ትንሣኤ የለም እያሉ ሰዱቃውያን ወደ እርሱ መጡ፤ ጠየቁትም፤ \v 24 እንዲህ እያሉ፦ «መምህር ሆይ፣ ሙሴ እንዲህ አለ፦ “ማንም ልጆች ሳይኖሩት ቢሞት፣ ወንድሙ ሚስቱን ያገባል፤ ለወንድሙም ዘር ያስነሣል።”
am.B: በዚያው ቀን ትንሣኤ የለም የሚሉ አንዳንድ ሰዱቃውያን ጥያቄ ይዘው ወደ እርሱ መጡ። \v 24 «መምህር ሆይ» አሉት፣ «ሙሴ ይህን ደንብ ሰጥቷል፦ “አንድ ሰው ልጆች ሳይተው ቢሞት፣ ወንድሙ የሞተውን ሰው ሚስት አግብቶ ለሟቹ ወንድሙ ዘር ይተካለት።”
am.R: በዚያው ቀን አንዳንድ ሰዱቃውያን ወደ ኢየሱስ መጡ። ሰዱቃውያን የሞቱ ሰዎች ተመልሰው ሕያው አይሆኑም ብለው ያስተምሩ ነበር። ኢየሱስንም አንድ ጥያቄ ጠየቁት። \v 24 እንዲህ አሉ፦ «መምህር ሆይ፣ ሙሴ በሕጉ እንዲህ ብሎ ጻፈ፦ “አንድ ሰው ልጆች ሳይኖሩት ቢሞት፣ ወንድሙ የሞተውን ሰው ሚስት ማግባት አለበት። ከዚያም የሚወለዱት ልጆች እንደ ሞተው ወንድም ልጆች ይቆጠራሉ።”

decisions.choice: Sadducees: a party of priests and leading families
decisions.reason: They held to the written law and rejected teachings not found there. They denied the resurrection and the existence of angels and spirits (Acts 23:8).

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 25:5-6: a brother marries the widow to give the dead man an heir
alternatives: a rule of the Sadducees' own
decisions.reason: The law kept a man's name and land in his family through his brother's children. The words "raise up offspring for his brother" echo Genesis 38:8.

decisions.choice: saying, without the article, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the ones who say, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add the article, so that the phrase describes the Sadducees as those who deny the resurrection. Without it, they come saying so. The sense is much the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: brother: no gender span
decisions.reason: The law speaks of a particular man's male brother who marries the widow, so the word takes no gender setting.

decisions.choice: wrote in the law; their children will count as the children of the brother who died
alternatives: said; raise up offspring for his brother
decisions.reason: Readable says where Moses said it and explains what raising up offspring for a brother meant.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns, pronouns before the verb and possessives (le, lo, su, tus)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the end of the verb ("responderle", "hacerle"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal; speech keeps its own tenses at every level
decisions.reason: As in John, Mark and Luke, and in Matthew 11: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading, while Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers now meet stories. The Sadducees' story of the seven brothers is speech, so it is in the passé composé at every level. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: les Sadducéens; Maître
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form, capitalised like the other Jewish groups, as in Mark 12:18; "Maître" for the address "Teacher", as in Mark 12:19 and 22:16, here and in 22:36.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yake, yeye, wangu, yako)
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("walimjia", "wakamwuliza"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This applies to the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "người Sa-đu-sê"; "sự sống lại" for resurrection (22:23-31)
decisions.reason: The wording of the parallel, Mark 12:18: "Sa-đu-sê" is the Protestant transliteration and "sự sống lại" the plain Bible word.

decisions.choice: "Thưa Thầy" for the Sadducees' "Teacher" (also 22:36); "anh em" for brother
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:19: they address him as a teacher; "anh em" names a brother without saying older or younger, which the law leaves open.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Matthew 22:23-46; the Sadducees speak to Jesus in 합쇼체 with "선생님"
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters; respect for Jesus is carried by -시- and 께서. The questioners are polite, as in the Korean Mark 12:19.

decisions.choice: "사두개파 사람들"; "부활" (L, B), described at Readable; "씨를 일으키다" (L)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 12:18-19. "형제" with no gender span: these are real brothers.

decisions.choice: o irmão dele, a mulher dele (L); o irmão dele, a viúva (B, R)
alternatives: o seu irmão, a sua mulher
decisions.reason: Three men and a woman are in the sentence, so "seu" and "sua" would leave the owner unclear. Portuguese says "dele", and Balanced and Readable name the widow, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans: plain "እርሱ" and the object suffix on the verb ("ጠየቁት")
alternatives: a capitalised pronoun, as the English alternative
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Christ has nothing to change in Amharic. The English spans in this passage have no Amharic counterpart.

decisions.choice: "ትንሣኤ" (resurrection)
decisions.reason: "ትንሣኤ" is the living Amharic word for the rising of the dead, used in church and in everyday speech. Readable says it plainly: the dead "ተመልሰው ሕያው አይሆኑም" (do not come back to life), as the English Readable explains it.

source.text: ἦσαν δὲ παρ’ ἡμῖν ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοί· καὶ ὁ πρῶτος γήμας ἐτελεύτησεν, καὶ μὴ ἔχων σπέρμα ἀφῆκεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: There were now among us seven brothers; and the first having married died, and not having offspring he left the wife of him to the brother of him;

en.L: Now there were seven brothers among us; and the first married and died, and having no offspring he left his wife to his brother.
en.B: There were seven brothers in our community. The first one married and died, and because he had no children, his widow went to his brother.
en.R: There were seven brothers who lived near us. The first brother got married, but he died. He had no children, so his brother married his wife.

es.L: Pues bien, con nosotros había siete hermanos; y el primero, tras casarse, falleció, y como no tenía descendencia, dejó a su esposa a su hermano.
es.B: En nuestra comunidad había siete hermanos. El primero se casó y murió, y como no tenía hijos, su viuda pasó a su hermano.
es.R: Había siete hermanos que vivían cerca de nosotros. El primero se casó, pero murió. No tenía hijos, así que su hermano se casó con la viuda.

fr.L: Or il y avait chez nous sept frères ; et le premier, s’étant marié, est mort, et, n’ayant pas de descendance, il a laissé sa femme à son frère.
fr.B: Il y avait dans notre communauté sept frères. Le premier s’est marié et il est mort ; comme il n’avait pas d’enfants, sa veuve est revenue à son frère.
fr.R: Il y avait sept frères qui vivaient près de chez nous. Le premier s’est marié, mais il est mort. Il n’avait pas d’enfants, alors son frère a épousé sa femme.

sw.L: Sasa palikuwa na ndugu saba miongoni mwetu; na yule wa kwanza, baada ya kuoa, alifariki, na kwa kuwa hakuwa na uzao, akamwacha mke wake kwa ndugu yake.
sw.B: Katika jamii yetu palikuwa na ndugu saba. Wa kwanza alioa kisha akafariki. Kwa kuwa hakuwa na watoto, mjane wake akawa mke wa ndugu yake.
sw.R: Kulikuwa na ndugu saba walioishi karibu nasi. Ndugu wa kwanza alioa, lakini akafa. Hakuwa na watoto, kwa hiyo ndugu yake akamwoa mke wake.

vi.L: Vậy, ở giữa chúng tôi có bảy anh em; người thứ nhất cưới vợ rồi chết, và vì không có dòng dõi, đã để vợ mình lại cho anh em mình.
vi.B: Ở chỗ chúng tôi có bảy anh em kia. Người đầu cưới vợ rồi chết. Vì không có con, người ấy để vợ lại cho anh em mình.
vi.R: Có bảy anh em trai sống gần chúng tôi. Người anh cả cưới vợ nhưng chết, không có con. Vì thế người em kế cưới người vợ góa ấy.

ko.L: 그런데 우리 가운데 일곱 형제가 있었습니다. 맏이가 장가를 들었다가 죽었는데, 씨가 없어서 자기 아내를 자기 형제에게 남겼습니다.
ko.B: 저희 가운데 일곱 형제가 있었습니다. 맏이가 장가를 들었다가 죽었는데, 자식이 없어서 그 아내가 그의 동생에게 넘어갔습니다.
ko.R: 저희 동네에 일곱 형제가 살았습니다. 맏형이 결혼했는데, 자식 없이 죽었습니다. 그래서 그 동생이 형의 아내와 결혼했습니다.

pt.L: Ora, havia entre nós sete irmãos; e o primeiro, tendo se casado, morreu e, não tendo descendência, deixou a mulher para o irmão dele.
pt.B: Havia sete irmãos na nossa comunidade. O primeiro se casou e morreu e, como não tinha filhos, a viúva dele ficou para o irmão.
pt.R: Havia sete irmãos que moravam perto de nós. O primeiro irmão se casou, mas morreu. Ele não tinha filhos, e por isso o irmão dele se casou com a viúva.

am.L: በእኛ ዘንድ ሰባት ወንድማማቾች ነበሩ፤ የመጀመሪያውም አግብቶ ሞተ፤ ዘርም ሳይኖረው ሚስቱን ለወንድሙ ተወ፤
am.B: በመካከላችን ሰባት ወንድማማቾች ነበሩ። የመጀመሪያው አግብቶ ሞተ፤ ልጆችም ስላልነበሩት ሚስቱ ለወንድሙ ሆነች።
am.R: በአጠገባችን የሚኖሩ ሰባት ወንድማማቾች ነበሩ። የመጀመሪያው ወንድም ሚስት አገባ፤ ግን ሞተ። ልጆች አልነበሩትም፤ ስለዚህ ወንድሙ ሚስቱን አገባት።

decisions.choice: among us: told as a real case
decisions.reason: They present it as something that happened. It may be a case invented to make belief in the resurrection look foolish.

decisions.choice: offspring: children
decisions.reason: The word means seed and is often used for descendants.

decisions.choice: "우리 가운데" (L); "저희 가운데" (B); "저희 동네에" (R)
decisions.reason: The case is told as real (meaning decision). Speaking politely to Jesus, "저희" is the humble "we"; Literal keeps the plain pronoun.

decisions.choice: "동생" (B, R) where the order of birth is told
decisions.reason: The brothers are counted in order from the eldest, so the next one is a younger brother.

source.text: ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ δεύτερος καὶ ὁ τρίτος, ἕως τῶν ἑπτά·

records.literal_gloss: Likewise also the second and the third, until the seven;

en.L: Likewise also the second and the third, up to the seventh.
en.B: The same thing happened to the second brother, and the third, and so on through all seven.
en.R: The same thing happened to the second brother and the third brother. It happened to all seven of them.

es.L: Del mismo modo también el segundo y el tercero, hasta el séptimo.
es.B: Lo mismo le pasó al segundo hermano, y al tercero, y así hasta los siete.
es.R: Lo mismo les pasó al segundo hermano y al tercero. Les pasó a los siete.

fr.L: De même aussi le deuxième et le troisième, jusqu’au septième.
fr.B: Il en a été de même pour le deuxième frère, puis pour le troisième, et ainsi de suite jusqu’au septième.
fr.R: La même chose est arrivée au deuxième frère et au troisième frère. C’est arrivé aux sept frères.

sw.L: Ndivyo ilivyokuwa pia kwa wa pili na wa tatu, mpaka wale saba.
sw.B: Jambo hilo hilo lilimtokea ndugu wa pili, na wa tatu, na hivyo hivyo mpaka wote saba.
sw.R: Jambo hilo hilo liliwapata ndugu wa pili na wa tatu. Liliwapata wote saba.

vi.L: Người thứ hai và người thứ ba cũng vậy, cho đến người thứ bảy.
vi.B: Người thứ hai, người thứ ba cũng vậy, cho đến cả bảy người.
vi.R: Người em thứ hai và người em thứ ba cũng chết như vậy. Cả bảy anh em đều như thế.

ko.L: 둘째도 셋째도 마찬가지로, 일곱째까지 [그러하였습니다].
ko.B: 둘째도 셋째도 그렇게 되어, 일곱째까지 다 그러했습니다.
ko.R: 둘째와 셋째에게도 똑같은 일이 일어났습니다. 일곱 형제가 모두 그렇게 되었습니다.

pt.L: Do mesmo modo também o segundo e o terceiro, até o sétimo.
pt.B: O mesmo aconteceu com o segundo irmão, e com o terceiro, e assim por diante, até o sétimo.
pt.R: O mesmo aconteceu com o segundo irmão e com o terceiro. Aconteceu com todos os sete.

am.L: እንዲሁም ደግሞ ሁለተኛውና ሦስተኛው፣ እስከ ሰባተኛው ድረስ።
am.B: በሁለተኛውም፣ በሦስተኛውም ወንድም ላይ እንዲሁ ሆነ፤ እስከ ሰባቱም ድረስ እንዲሁ ቀጠለ።
am.R: በሁለተኛውና በሦስተኛው ወንድም ላይም እንዲሁ ሆነ። በሰባቱም ላይ እንዲሁ ሆነ።

decisions.choice: up to the seventh: each of the seven in turn
decisions.reason: The phrase means the pattern went on through all seven brothers.

decisions.choice: [그러하였습니다] (L)
decisions.reason: Korean needs a verb to end the sentence.

source.text: ὕστερον δὲ πάντων ἀπέθανεν ἡ γυνή.

records.literal_gloss: Last then of all died the woman.

en.L: And last of all the woman died.
en.B: Finally, after them all, the woman died.
en.R: Last of all, the woman died too.

es.L: Y al final de todos murió la mujer.
es.B: Por último, después de todos ellos, murió la mujer.
es.R: Al final, la mujer también murió.

fr.L: Et après eux tous, la femme est morte.
fr.B: Finalement, après eux tous, la femme est morte.
fr.R: Enfin, la femme est morte, elle aussi.

sw.L: Na baada ya wote, alikufa yule mwanamke.
sw.B: Hatimaye, baada ya wote, yule mwanamke naye akafariki.
sw.R: Mwishowe, yule mwanamke naye akafa.

vi.L: Và sau cùng hết, người đàn bà cũng chết.
vi.B: Sau cùng, người đàn bà ấy cũng chết.
vi.R: Cuối cùng, người đàn bà ấy cũng chết.

ko.L: 그리고 모든 [사람] 가운데 마지막으로 그 여자도 죽었습니다.
ko.B: 맨 나중에는 그 여자도 죽었습니다.
ko.R: 마지막에는 그 여자도 죽었습니다.

pt.L: E, por último de todos, morreu a mulher.
pt.B: Por fim, depois de todos eles, a mulher morreu.
pt.R: Por último, a mulher também morreu.

am.L: ከሁሉም በኋላ ደግሞ ሴቲቱ ሞተች።
am.B: በመጨረሻም፣ ከሁሉም በኋላ ሴቲቱ ሞተች።
am.R: በመጨረሻ ሴቲቱም ሞተች።

source.text: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει οὖν τίνος τῶν ἑπτὰ ἔσται γυνή;

records.literal_gloss: In the resurrection therefore of which of the seven will she be wife?

en.L: In the resurrection, then, of which of the seven will she be [the] wife?
en.B: So when the dead are raised, which of the seven will have her as his wife?
en.R: So when people rise from death, which of the seven brothers will she be married to?

es.L: En la resurrección, pues, ¿de cuál de los siete será esposa?
es.B: Así que, cuando los muertos resuciten, ¿de cuál de los siete será esposa?
es.R: Entonces, cuando la gente vuelva de la muerte, ¿con cuál de los siete hermanos estará casada?

fr.L: À la résurrection, donc, duquel des sept sera-t-elle la femme ?
fr.B: Alors, quand les morts se relèveront, lequel des sept l’aura pour femme ?
fr.R: Alors, quand les morts reviendront à la vie, avec lequel des sept frères sera-t-elle mariée ?

sw.L: Katika ufufuo, basi, mke wa nani kati ya hao saba atakuwa?
sw.B: Basi wafu watakapofufuliwa, ni yupi kati ya wale saba atakayekuwa naye kama mke wake?
sw.R: Basi watu watakapofufuka kutoka kwa wafu, atakuwa ameolewa na ndugu yupi kati ya wale saba?

vi.L: Vậy trong sự sống lại, bà ấy sẽ là vợ của ai trong bảy người?
vi.B: Vậy khi người chết sống lại, bà ấy sẽ là vợ của ai trong bảy người?
vi.R: Vậy khi người chết sống lại, bà ấy sẽ là vợ của người nào trong bảy anh em?

ko.L: 그러면 부활 때에 그 여자는 일곱 가운데 누구의 아내가 되겠습니까?
ko.B: 그러면 죽은 사람들이 살아날 때에, 그 여자는 일곱 형제 가운데 누구의 아내가 되겠습니까?
ko.R: 그러면 죽은 사람들이 다시 살아날 때, 그 여자는 일곱 형제 가운데 누구의 아내가 됩니까?

pt.L: Na ressurreição, então, de qual dos sete ela será esposa?
pt.B: Então, quando os mortos forem ressuscitados, qual dos sete a terá como esposa?
pt.R: Então, quando as pessoas voltarem a viver, com qual dos sete irmãos ela vai estar casada?

am.L: እንግዲህ በትንሣኤ ከሰባቱ የማንኛው ሚስት ትሆናለች?
am.B: ታዲያ ሙታን በሚነሡበት ጊዜ ከሰባቱ የትኛው ሚስት ትሆናለች?
am.R: ታዲያ ሰዎች ከሞት በሚነሡበት ጊዜ ከሰባቱ ወንድሞች የማን ሚስት ትሆናለች?

decisions.choice: in the resurrection: when the dead are raised at the last day
decisions.reason: The phrase names the time when God raises the dead (Daniel 12:2). The Sadducees speak of it to mock it.

decisions.choice: when the dead are raised (B); when people rise from death (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the resurrection is.

decisions.choice: "부활" (L); "죽은 사람들이 살아날 때" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English Balanced says it as an event; "부활" stays at Literal.

source.text: πάντες γὰρ ἔσχον αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: All for had her.

en.L: For all [seven] had her."
en.B: All of them were married to her."
en.R: All seven of them had been her husband."

es.L: Porque todos [los siete] la tuvieron».
es.B: Todos estuvieron casados con ella».
es.R: Los siete habían sido su esposo».

fr.L: Car tous l’ont eue [pour femme]. »
fr.B: Ils ont tous été mariés avec elle. »
fr.R: Les sept frères ont tous été son mari ! »

sw.L: Kwa kuwa wote [saba] walikuwa naye [kama mke]."
sw.B: Wote walikuwa wamemwoa."
sw.R: Wote saba walikuwa waume zake."

vi.L: Vì cả [bảy] người đều đã lấy bà ấy."
vi.B: Vì cả bảy người đều đã cưới bà ấy làm vợ."
vi.R: Vì cả bảy anh em đều đã từng là chồng của bà ấy!"

ko.L: 모두가 그 여자를 [아내로] 맞았으니 말입니다."
ko.B: 일곱 형제가 다 그 여자를 아내로 맞았으니 말입니다."
ko.R: 일곱 형제가 모두 그 여자의 남편이었으니 말입니다."

pt.L: Pois todos [os sete] a tiveram."
pt.B: Todos eles foram casados com ela."
pt.R: Os sete foram marido dela."

am.L: ሁሉም [ሚስት አድርገው] ይዘዋት ነበርና።»
am.B: ሁሉም አግብተዋት ነበርና።»
am.R: ሰባቱም ባሎቿ ሆነው ነበር።»

decisions.choice: had her: had her as a wife
decisions.reason: To have a woman means to be married to her (14:4).

decisions.choice: "[아내로] 맞았으니" (L)
decisions.reason: "Had her" means had her as wife (meaning decision); Korean needs the word.

source.text: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ θεοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Answering then Jesus said to them, You err not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God;

en.L: But Jesus answered them, "You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures or the power of God.
en.B: Jesus replied, "You have gone astray, because you understand neither the Scriptures nor God's power.
en.R: Jesus answered them, "You are wrong! You do not understand what the Scriptures say. And you do not know how powerful God is.

es.L: Pero respondiendo Jesús, les dijo: «{{plural_you:Están|Estáis}} equivocados, no conociendo las Escrituras ni el poder de Dios.
es.B: Jesús les contestó: «{{plural_you:Andan|Andáis}} descarriados, porque no {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}} ni las Escrituras ni el poder de Dios.
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «¡{{plural_you:Están|Estáis}} equivocados! No {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}} lo que dicen las Escrituras. Y no {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} cuán poderoso es Dios.

fr.L: Jésus, prenant la parole, leur dit : « Vous vous égarez, ne connaissant ni les Écritures ni la puissance de Dieu.
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Vous êtes dans l’erreur, parce que vous ne comprenez ni les Écritures ni la puissance de Dieu.
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Vous vous trompez ! Vous ne comprenez pas ce que disent les Écritures. Et vous ne savez pas combien Dieu est puissant.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu, akijibu, aliwaambia, "Mnakosea, bila kuyajua Maandiko wala nguvu ya Mungu.
sw.B: Yesu akawajibu, "Mmepotoka, kwa sababu hamyaelewi Maandiko wala uwezo wa Mungu.
sw.R: Yesu akawajibu, "Mmekosea kabisa! Hamwelewi Maandiko yanasema nini. Tena hamjui jinsi Mungu alivyo na nguvu nyingi.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu đáp lời và nói với họ: "Các người lầm lạc, vì không biết Kinh Thánh, cũng không biết quyền năng của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Các người lầm rồi, vì các người không hiểu Kinh Thánh, cũng không hiểu quyền năng của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Các người sai rồi! Các người không hiểu Kinh Thánh nói gì. Các người cũng không biết quyền năng của Đức Chúa Trời lớn đến đâu.

ko.L: 예수께서 대답하여 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 성경도 하나님의 능력도 알지 못하여 잘못 생각하고 있다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "너희는 성경도 모르고 하나님의 능력도 모르기 때문에 잘못 생각하고 있다.
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "너희는 잘못 알고 있다. 너희는 성경이 무엇을 말하는지 모른다. 또 하나님께서 얼마나 큰 능력을 가지셨는지도 모른다.

pt.L: Respondendo, Jesus lhes disse: "Vocês estão enganados, não conhecendo as Escrituras nem o poder de Deus.
pt.B: Jesus respondeu: "Vocês se desviaram, porque não entendem nem as Escrituras nem o poder de Deus.
pt.R: Jesus respondeu a eles: "Vocês estão errados! Vocês não entendem o que as Escrituras dizem. E não sabem como Deus é poderoso.

am.L: ኢየሱስ ግን መልሶ እንዲህ አላቸው፦ «መጻሕፍትን ወይም የእግዚአብሔርን ኃይል ስለማታውቁ ትስታላችሁ።
am.B: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ሲል መለሰላቸው፦ «መጻሕፍትንም ሆነ የእግዚአብሔርን ኃይል ስለማታስተውሉ ከእውነት ርቃችኋል።
am.R: ኢየሱስም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰላቸው፦ «ተሳስታችኋል! መጻሕፍት የሚሉትን አታስተውሉም። እግዚአብሔር ምን ያህል ኃያል እንደ ሆነም አታውቁም።

decisions.choice: you are mistaken: you have wandered from the truth
decisions.reason: The verb means to go astray. It can be passive, "you are led astray", but the sense here is that they are in error.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures and the power of God: both answered in what follows
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of God's power in 22:30, where the raised do not marry, and of the Scriptures in 22:31-32.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" (Están|Estáis, entienden|entendéis)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: "lầm lạc" (L); "lầm" (B); "sai" (R); "các người" for the Sadducees
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:24: "lầm lạc" keeps the picture of wandering from the truth that the meaning decision describes; Jesus speaks to opponents as "các người".

decisions.choice: "잘못 생각하다" (L, B); "잘못 알다" (R) for planasthe
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 12:24.

decisions.choice: "መጻሕፍት" (the Scriptures)
decisions.reason: In Jesus's mouth "the writings" already means the Scriptures, and Amharic readers hear "መጻሕፍት" so; the Greek has no "holy" here.

source.text: ἐν γὰρ τῇ ἀναστάσει οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἄγγελοι θεοῦ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ εἰσιν·

records.literal_gloss: In for the resurrection neither do they marry nor are given in marriage, but like angels of God in heaven they are.

en.L: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like angels of God in heaven.
en.B: For once the dead are raised, men no longer take wives and women are no longer given as brides; they are like the angels of God in heaven.
en.R: After people rise from death, they do not get married. They are like God's angels in heaven.

es.L: Porque en la resurrección ni se casan ni se les da en matrimonio, sino que son como ángeles de Dios en el cielo.
es.B: Porque, una vez resucitados los muertos, los hombres ya no toman esposa ni las mujeres son dadas como novias; son como los ángeles de Dios en el cielo.
es.R: Después de volver de la muerte, la gente no se casa. Son como los ángeles de Dios en el cielo.

fr.L: Car à la résurrection, ils ne se marient pas et ne sont pas donnés en mariage, mais ils sont comme des anges de Dieu dans le ciel.
fr.B: Car une fois que les morts se sont relevés, les hommes ne prennent plus de femme et les femmes ne sont plus données en mariage ; ils sont comme les anges de Dieu dans le ciel.
fr.R: Quand les gens seront revenus à la vie, ils ne se marieront pas. Ils seront comme les anges de Dieu dans le ciel.

decisions.choice: marry and are given in marriage: men took wives, and fathers gave their daughters
alternatives: two names for the same act
decisions.reason: The two verbs describe the man's part and the bride's. Neither happens after the resurrection.

decisions.choice: like angels: in not marrying, not in becoming angels
decisions.reason: Raised people do not die (Luke 20:36), so marriage to provide heirs is no longer needed. Jesus also affirms the angels the Sadducees denied (Acts 23:8).

decisions.choice: of God, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: like angels in heaven, the reading of some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts lack "of God", and others have "angels of God". The meaning does not change. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: men no longer take wives and women are no longer given as brides
alternatives: they neither marry nor are given in marriage
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out the two sides the verbs describe.

decisions.choice: "cưới ... được gả" (L); "cưới vợ hay gả chồng" (B)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:25: Vietnamese has the same pair as the Greek, a man "cưới" a wife and a daughter "được gả" by her father, the custom the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: "장가가다" and "시집가다" (L, B); "결혼하다" (R)
decisions.reason: Men took wives and women were given in marriage (meaning decision); Korean has a verb for each, as in the Korean Mark 12:25.

decisions.choice: "አያገቡም" ... "አይዳሩም" (they do not take wives ... are not given as brides)
alternatives: "አይጋቡም" (they do not marry each other) for both
decisions.reason: Amharic has the same pair the Greek has: a man "ያገባል" (takes a wife) and a woman "ትዳራለች" (is given in marriage by her family), so both verbs come through without explanation.

decisions.choice: spoken to you by God: God's word to Moses speaks to them too
decisions.reason: Scripture is God speaking to each generation that reads it, the Sadducees included.

decisions.choice: have you not read: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: As in 12:3, Jesus asks whether they have understood what they read. The Sadducees held the books of Moses in the highest honor.

decisions.choice: He said
decisions.reason: Readable ends the question and begins a new sentence for God's words. At the start of a sentence the pronoun is capitalized either way.

decisions.choice: "phán" for God speaking
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "phán" for God and "nói" for every other speaker, Jesus included (Settled); as in Mark 12:26.

decisions.choice: "그분이 말씀하시기를," (L); a separate sentence introducing the quotation (B, R)
alternatives: one question running into the quotation at every level
decisions.reason: The quotation completes the question (meaning decision); Korean cannot put a question mark after a quotation that ends in a statement of God, so Balanced and Readable close the question first.

decisions.choice: the question ends here, and "saying" becomes a short clause introducing the quotation ("እንዲህ ይላል፦")
alternatives: the question closing after the quotation in 22:32, as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: An Amharic question ends with its verb, so the verb "have you not read" cannot wait until after the quotation. The question closes here, and God's words follow as what the passage says.

decisions.choice: Exodus 3:6: God speaks to Moses from the bush
decisions.reason: God named himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob centuries after their deaths (also Exodus 3:15-16). Jesus quotes the law of Moses, which the Sadducees accepted.

decisions.choice: I am: God is still their God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Exodus 3:6 has no verb; the argument rests on God calling himself their God long after they died. A God of the living does not bind himself to those who have ceased to be.

decisions.choice: a question mark at the end: the quotation completes the question of 22:31
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates the whole of 22:31-32a as one question.

decisions.choice: statement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable made 22:31 a complete question, so the quotation ends as a statement.

decisions.choice: the question closed with "sao?" after the quotation (L, B)
decisions.reason: The quotation completes the question of 22:31 (meaning decision); Vietnamese marks a question with a final particle, so "sao" closes it here.

decisions.choice: [하지 않으셨느냐]? (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek's question mark closes the question begun in 22:31 (meaning decision); Korean needs a verb to carry it, so Literal adds "did he not say" in brackets.

pt.R: As pessoas que ouviram isso ficaram admiradas com o que Jesus ensinava.

am.L: ሕዝቡም ሰምተው በትምህርቱ ተደነቁ።
am.B: ትምህርቱን የሰሙት ሕዝብ በጣም ተደነቁ።
am.R: ይህን የሰሙ ሰዎች ኢየሱስ ባስተማረው ነገር ተገረሙ።

decisions.choice: astounded: struck with amazement
decisions.reason: As at the end of the Sermon on the Mount (7:28), the crowds are amazed at his teaching.

decisions.choice: O ensino {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}
alternatives: O seu ensino, with no span
decisions.reason: The English Balanced opens with "His", which is capitalised either way and takes no span. Portuguese puts the owner after the noun, "dele", so it carries the setting.

source.text: Οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ἐφίμωσεν τοὺς Σαδδουκαίους συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.

records.literal_gloss: The but Pharisees having heard that he had silenced the Sadducees were gathered together at the same.

en.L: But the Pharisees, hearing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had silenced the Sadducees, gathered together.
en.B: The Pharisees heard that Jesus had put the Sadducees to silence, and they came together in one place.
en.R: The Pharisees heard that Jesus had answered the Sadducees so well that they could say nothing more. So the Pharisees met together.

es.L: Pero los fariseos, al oír que había dejado sin palabra a los saduceos, se reunieron en un mismo lugar.
es.B: Los fariseos se enteraron de que Jesús había hecho callar a los saduceos, y se reunieron en un solo lugar.
es.R: Los fariseos oyeron que Jesús había respondido tan bien a los saduceos que estos ya no pudieron decir nada más. Entonces los fariseos se reunieron.

fr.L: Mais les Pharisiens, ayant appris qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait réduit au silence les Sadducéens, se rassemblèrent au même [lieu].
fr.B: Les Pharisiens apprirent que Jésus avait fermé la bouche aux Sadducéens, et ils se rassemblèrent.
fr.R: Les Pharisiens ont appris que Jésus avait si bien répondu aux Sadducéens qu’ils n’avaient plus rien pu dire. Alors les Pharisiens se sont réunis.

sw.L: Lakini Mafarisayo, waliposikia kwamba amewanyamazisha Masadukayo, walikutana mahali pamoja.
sw.B: Mafarisayo waliposikia kwamba Yesu amewanyamazisha Masadukayo, walikutanika mahali pamoja.
sw.R: Mafarisayo walisikia kwamba Yesu aliwajibu Masadukayo vizuri sana hata wakakosa la kusema. Basi Mafarisayo wakakutana pamoja.

vi.L: Nhưng những người Pha-ri-si nghe rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm cho những người Sa-đu-sê câm miệng, thì họp nhau lại.
vi.B: Khi những người Pha-ri-si nghe Đức Giê-xu đã làm cho những người Sa-đu-sê phải im tiếng, họ họp nhau lại.
vi.R: Những người Pha-ri-si nghe rằng Đức Giê-xu đã trả lời những người Sa-đu-sê hay đến nỗi họ không còn gì để nói. Vì thế những người Pha-ri-si họp nhau lại.

ko.L: 그런데 바리새파 사람들은 그분이 사두개파 사람들의 말문을 막으셨다는 것을 듣고 한곳에 모였다.
ko.B: 예수께서 사두개파 사람들의 말문을 막으셨다는 소식을 듣고, 바리새파 사람들이 한자리에 모였다.
ko.R: 바리새파 사람들은 예수께서 사두개파 사람들에게 훌륭하게 대답하셔서, 그들이 더 아무 말도 못 하게 되었다는 소식을 들었다. 그래서 바리새파 사람들이 함께 모였다.

pt.L: Mas os fariseus, ouvindo que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha feito calar os saduceus, reuniram-se no mesmo lugar.
pt.B: Os fariseus souberam que Jesus tinha feito os saduceus se calarem e se reuniram num só lugar.
pt.R: Os fariseus souberam que Jesus tinha respondido tão bem aos saduceus que eles não conseguiram dizer mais nada. Então os fariseus se reuniram.

am.L: ፈሪሳውያን ግን ሰዱቃውያንን ዝም እንዳሰኛቸው ሰምተው በአንድ ላይ ተሰበሰቡ።
am.B: ፈሪሳውያንም ኢየሱስ ሰዱቃውያንን ዝም እንዳሰኛቸው ሰሙ፤ በአንድ ስፍራም ተሰበሰቡ።
am.R: ፈሪሳውያን ኢየሱስ ለሰዱቃውያን ሌላ ምንም ሊናገሩ እስከማይችሉ ድረስ በሚገባ እንደ መለሰላቸው ሰሙ። ስለዚህ ፈሪሳውያን አንድ ላይ ተሰበሰቡ።

decisions.choice: silenced: left with nothing to say
decisions.reason: The verb means to muzzle. It is used of the guest without wedding clothes (22:12).

decisions.choice: gathered together: perhaps an echo of Psalm 2:2
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament of Psalm 2:2 the rulers are "gathered together" against the LORD and his anointed, in the same words. Whether Matthew intends the echo is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: "말문을 막다" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Silenced, left with nothing to say (meaning decision); the same verb as the speechless guest in 22:12, "말문이 막혔다".

source.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν νομικὸς πειράζων αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: And questioned one of them, a lawyer, testing him:

en.L: And one of them, a lawyer, questioned [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], testing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}:
en.B: One of their number, a man trained in the law, put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to test {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}:
en.R: One of them knew the law of Moses very well. He wanted to test Jesus, so he asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a question.

es.L: Y uno de ellos, un experto en la ley, preguntó, poniéndolo a prueba:
es.B: Uno de ellos, un experto en la ley, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hizo una pregunta para ponerlo a prueba:
es.R: Uno de ellos conocía muy bien la ley de Moisés. Quería poner a prueba a Jesús, así que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hizo una pregunta.

fr.L: Et l’un d’eux, un expert de la Loi, [{{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}]interrogea pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettre à l’épreuve :
fr.B: L’un d’eux, un expert de la Loi, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} posa une question pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettre à l’épreuve :
fr.R: L’un d’eux était un spécialiste de la Loi de Dieu. Il voulait mettre Jésus à l’épreuve, alors il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a posé une question.

sw.L: Na mmoja kati yao, mtaalamu wa sheria, alimhoji, akimjaribu:
sw.B: Mmoja wao, mtaalamu wa sheria, alimwuliza swali ili kumjaribu:
sw.R: Mmoja wao aliijua sheria ya Musa vizuri sana. Alitaka kumjaribu Yesu, kwa hiyo akamwuliza swali.

vi.L: Và một người trong họ, là một chuyên gia luật pháp, hỏi [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] để thử {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}:
vi.B: Một người trong nhóm họ, là một chuyên gia luật pháp, hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một câu để thử {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}:
vi.R: Một người trong số họ rất thông thạo luật pháp Môi-se. Ông muốn thử Đức Giê-xu, nên hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một câu:

ko.L: 그리고 그들 가운데 한 사람인 율법 전문가가 그분을 시험하여 물었다.
ko.B: 그들 가운데 율법 전문가 한 사람이 예수를 시험하려고 물었다.
ko.R: 그들 가운데 한 사람은 하나님의 율법을 잘 아는 사람이었다. 그는 예수를 시험해 보려고 질문했다.

pt.L: E um deles, um especialista na Lei, perguntou, pondo-{{deity_pronoun:o|O}} à prova:
pt.B: Um deles, um estudioso da Lei, {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} fez uma pergunta para testá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}:
pt.R: Um deles conhecia muito bem a Lei de Moisés. Ele queria pôr Jesus à prova. Por isso, fez uma pergunta a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.

am.L: ከእነርሱም አንዱ የሕግ አዋቂ እየፈተነው ጠየቀው፦
am.B: ከመካከላቸውም የሕግ አዋቂ የሆነ አንድ ሰው ሊፈትነው ፈልጎ እንዲህ ሲል ጠየቀው፦
am.R: ከእነርሱ መካከል አንዱ የሙሴን ሕግ በደንብ የሚያውቅ ሰው ነበር። እርሱ ኢየሱስን ሊፈትነው ፈለገ፤ ስለዚህ አንድ ጥያቄ ጠየቀው፦

decisions.choice: lawyer: an expert in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word names a scholar of the law, much like a scribe. It appears only here in Matthew.

decisions.choice: testing: putting him to a test
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 22:18. In Matthew the Pharisees' testing is meant to catch Jesus out (16:1; 19:3).

decisions.choice: a lawyer, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: one of them, without "a lawyer", the reading of a few witnesses
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts and early translations lack the word, and some think it was added from Luke 10:25. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a man trained in the law (B); knew the law of Moses very well (R)
decisions.reason: Today "lawyer" suggests a courtroom. Balanced and Readable say what kind of expert he was.

decisions.choice: un experto en la ley
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for this word (meaning decision m1): a man trained in the law of Moses. "Abogado" would suggest a modern lawyer in court.

decisions.choice: un expert de la Loi (L, B); un spécialiste de la Loi de Dieu (R)
alternatives: un homme qui connaissait très bien la Loi de Moïse (R)
decisions.reason: The settled forms for this word in the Gospels, as Luke 7:30 and 11:45: "légiste" now means a jurist or a forensic doctor, and "docteur" suggests medicine, as English "lawyer" suggests courts (m1). It is not the word for the scribes, who are "les scribes" (L, B).

decisions.choice: mtaalamu wa sheria
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for this word (meaning decision m1): a man trained in the law of Moses. "Mwanasheria" today means a lawyer in the courts.

decisions.choice: "chuyên gia luật pháp" (L, B); "rất thông thạo luật pháp Môi-se" (R) for the lawyer
decisions.reason: The wording of the Vietnamese Luke 10:25 and 11:45: an expert in the law of Moses (meaning decision); "luật sư" would suggest a modern advocate in court.

decisions.choice: "율법 전문가" (L, B); "하나님의 율법을 잘 아는 사람" (R) for nomikos
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Luke 10:25: a different word from the scribes ("율법학자"). The parallel Mark 12:28 has a scribe.

decisions.choice: um especialista na Lei (L); um estudioso da Lei (B); conhecia muito bem a Lei de Moisés (R)
decisions.reason: "Advogado" is a courtroom lawyer today, and "doutor da Lei" sounds like an academic title. Literal and Balanced say plainly that he was an expert in the Law of Moses; Readable says what that means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: perguntou, with no object
decisions.reason: Portuguese "perguntar" stands without an object, so Literal needs no bracketed pronoun where the English supplies [him].

decisions.choice: "የሕግ አዋቂ" (an expert in the law) for the lawyer
alternatives: "የሕግ መምህር" (teacher of the law, kept for the scribes)
decisions.reason: "ጠበቃ" is a modern courtroom lawyer, which this man was not. "የሕግ መምህራን" renders the scribes in Balanced and Readable, so a different phrase keeps the two Greek words apart.

source.text: Διδάσκαλε, ποία ἐντολὴ μεγάλη ἐν τῷ νόμῳ;

records.literal_gloss: Teacher, which commandment great in the law?

en.L: "Teacher, which commandment [is] great in the law?"
en.B: "Teacher, which commandment in the law ranks highest?"
en.R: "Teacher, which command in the law of Moses is the most important?"

es.L: «Maestro, ¿qué mandamiento [es] grande en la ley?».
es.B: «Maestro, ¿qué mandamiento de la ley ocupa el primer lugar?».
es.R: «Maestro, ¿cuál es el mandamiento más importante de la ley de Moisés?».

fr.L: « Maître, quel commandement [est] grand dans la Loi ? »
fr.B: « Maître, quel commandement de la Loi passe avant tous les autres ? »
fr.R: « Maître, dans la Loi de Moïse, quel est le commandement le plus important ? »

sw.L: "Mwalimu, amri ipi [ni] kuu katika sheria?"
sw.B: "Mwalimu, katika sheria ni amri gani inayotangulia zote?"
sw.R: "Mwalimu, katika sheria ya Musa, amri ipi ni ya muhimu kuliko zote?"

vi.L: "Thưa Thầy, điều răn nào lớn trong luật pháp?"
vi.B: "Thưa Thầy, trong luật pháp, điều răn nào là lớn nhất?"
vi.R: "Thưa Thầy, trong luật pháp Môi-se, điều răn nào quan trọng nhất?"

ko.L: "선생님, 율법에서 어느 계명이 큽니까?"
ko.B: "선생님, 율법에서 가장 큰 계명은 어느 것입니까?"
ko.R: "선생님, 모세의 율법에 있는 계명 가운데 어느 것이 가장 중요합니까?"

pt.L: "Mestre, qual mandamento [é] grande na Lei?"
pt.B: "Mestre, qual é o maior mandamento da Lei?"
pt.R: "Mestre, qual é o mandamento mais importante da Lei de Moisés?"

am.L: «መምህር ሆይ፣ በሕግ ውስጥ የትኛው ትእዛዝ ታላቅ [ነው]?»
am.B: «መምህር ሆይ፣ በሕጉ ውስጥ ከሁሉ የሚበልጠው ትእዛዝ የትኛው ነው?»
am.R: «መምህር ሆይ፣ በሙሴ ሕግ ውስጥ ከሁሉ ይበልጥ አስፈላጊው ትእዛዝ የትኛው ነው?»

decisions.choice: great: the greatest
decisions.reason: The plain form "great" often has the force of "greatest" in the Greek of the time.

decisions.choice: a common question: which command carries the most weight
decisions.reason: Jewish teachers discussed heavier and lighter commands (compare 23:23). Later tradition counted 613 commands in the law.

decisions.choice: ranks highest (B); most important (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the plain form.

decisions.choice: "điều răn" at every level; "luật pháp" in lowercase
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:28 and the style guide: "điều răn" is the familiar word for God's commandments, and "luật pháp" is lowercase as "law" is in English.

decisions.choice: "계명" at every level; "크다" (L), "가장 큰" (B), "가장 중요한" (R)
decisions.reason: "Great" here means the greatest (meaning decision); Literal keeps the Greek's plain adjective.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου·

records.literal_gloss: He and said to him, You shall love Lord the God of you with all the heart of you and with all the soul of you and with all the mind of you;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "'You shall love [the] Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.'
en.B: Jesus answered him, "'Love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, and with your whole mind.'
en.R: Jesus answered, "'Love the Lord your God with all of your heart. Love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all of your soul and with all of your mind.'

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le dijo: «“Amarás [al] Señor tu Dios de todo tu corazón y de toda tu alma y de toda tu mente”.
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «“Ama al Señor tu Dios con tu corazón entero, con tu alma entera y con tu mente entera”.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «“Ama al Señor tu Dios con todo tu corazón. Ámalo con toda tu alma y con toda tu mente”.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « “Tu aimeras le Seigneur ton Dieu de tout ton cœur, et de toute ton âme, et de toute ta pensée.”
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « “Aime le Seigneur ton Dieu de tout ton cœur, de toute ton âme et de tout ton esprit.”
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « “Aime le Seigneur ton Dieu de tout ton cœur. Aime-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} de toute ton âme et de toute ton intelligence.”

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "'Utampenda Bwana Mungu wako kwa moyo wako wote na kwa nafsi yako yote na kwa akili yako yote.'
sw.B: Yesu akamjibu, "'Mpende Bwana Mungu wako kwa moyo wako mzima, kwa nafsi yako nzima, na kwa akili yako nzima.'
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "'Mpende Bwana Mungu wako kwa moyo wako mzima. Mpende kwa nafsi yako yote na kwa akili yako yote.'

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với ông: "'Ngươi phải yêu thương Chúa, Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, với cả tấm lòng ngươi, với cả linh hồn ngươi, và với cả trí óc ngươi.'
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "'Ngươi phải yêu thương Chúa, Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, bằng cả tấm lòng, cả linh hồn và cả trí óc của ngươi.'
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "'Hãy yêu thương Chúa, Đức Chúa Trời của mình, hết lòng. Hãy yêu thương {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hết linh hồn và hết trí óc.'

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그에게 말씀하셨다. "'너는 너의 온 마음으로, 너의 온 목숨으로, 너의 온 생각으로 주 너의 하나님을 사랑할 것이다.'
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "'너는 온 마음과 온 목숨과 온 생각을 다하여 주 너의 하나님을 사랑하여라.'
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "'온 마음을 다하여 주 너의 하나님을 사랑하여라. 온 목숨과 온 생각을 다하여 그분을 사랑하여라.'

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhe disse: "'Amarás o Senhor, teu Deus, com todo o teu coração, e com toda a tua alma, e com toda a tua mente.'
pt.B: Jesus lhe respondeu: "'Amarás o Senhor, teu Deus, com todo o teu coração, com toda a tua alma e com toda a tua mente.'
pt.R: Jesus respondeu: "'Ama o Senhor, teu Deus, com todo o teu coração. Ama-{{deity_pronoun:o|O}} com toda a tua alma e com toda a tua mente.'

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 6:5, part of the Shema
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 6:4-9 was recited daily by devout Jews. Deuteronomy has heart, soul and strength; Matthew has mind in place of strength, and Mark 12:30 has all four.

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy 6:5 the Hebrew has God's name, which the Greek Old Testament gives as "Lord". As in 4:7 and 4:10.

decisions.choice: heart, soul and mind: the whole person
alternatives: three separate parts of a person
decisions.reason: Heart is the inner self, soul is life itself, and mind is thought and understanding. Together they mean love with all one is.

decisions.choice: Love (B, R)
decisions.reason: The future tense gives a command. Balanced and Readable use the plain command form, as in 5:43.

decisions.choice: Love him
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the verb to keep the sentences short.

decisions.choice: ta pensée (L); ton esprit (B); ton intelligence (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:30: the word means the mind, the power to think. Literal keeps the close "pensée"; Balanced says "esprit", the usual French for the mind as a faculty; Readable says "intelligence", the plainest word. "De tout ton cœur" is the French idiom for the Greek "with all".

decisions.choice: nafsi (soul)
decisions.reason: The word is the soul as a person's inner life, one of the three words for the whole person (meaning decision m3). "Roho" is also the word for the Spirit and for breath; "nafsi" keeps the sense of the self.

decisions.choice: "Chúa", not the divine-name setting, in the words of Deuteronomy 6:5
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:30: the Greek has kyrios, so Vietnamese writes "Chúa" as the English writes "Lord"; the meaning decision notes the divine name in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "ngươi" for the one addressed in the commandment (L, B); Readable uses the reflexive "mình"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:30: the solemn address of the law, not rude in this register; Readable avoids the archaic word.

decisions.choice: "주 너의 하나님" with no divine_name span; "마음", "목숨", "생각"; "사랑할 것이다" (L), "사랑하여라" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has kyrios, so the Korean says "주", as in the Korean Mark 12:30; the three words are those of Mark's Korean.

decisions.choice: tu: Amarás ... teu Deus, teu coração (L, B); Ama ... teu (R)
alternatives: você: Ame o Senhor, o seu Deus
decisions.reason: For the whole book: a commandment of the law is God speaking to a person, so it takes "tu" (style section 4). Balanced keeps the future "Amarás", the form in which Portuguese states commandments, which reads as a command and not a prediction; Readable uses the plain imperative "Ama", as the English Balanced and Readable say "Love".

decisions.choice: "በሙሉ ልብህ ... በሙሉ አእምሮህ" (with your whole heart ... your whole mind)
decisions.reason: "አእምሮ" is the everyday word for the mind that thinks and understands, which is the sense of the Greek word. The familiar "በፍጹም ... አሳብህ" is the wording of an existing Amharic Bible and is not reused. Literal keeps the Greek future "ትወዳለህ" (you shall love); Balanced and Readable give the command "ውደድ".

pt.L: Este é o grande e primeiro mandamento.
pt.B: Este é o grande mandamento, o primeiro de todos.
pt.R: Este é o mandamento mais importante. Ele vem em primeiro lugar.

am.L: ይህ ታላቁና የመጀመሪያው ትእዛዝ ነው።
am.B: ይህ ትእዛዝ ታላቅ ነው፤ ከሁሉም የመጀመሪያው ነው።

decisions.choice: first: first in rank

records.literal_gloss: Second and like it: You shall love the neighbor of you as yourself.

en.L: And [the] second [is] like it: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.'
en.B: A second command is of the same kind: 'Love your neighbor as you love yourself.'

decisions.choice: Leviticus 19:18: love your neighbor
decisions.reason: Jesus quoted it in 5:43 and 19:19. In Leviticus the neighbor is a fellow Israelite; Jesus extends love even to enemies (5:44).

decisions.choice: like it: of the same kind, also a command to love
decisions.reason: Both commands begin with the same verb. Love for neighbor flows from love for God and is bound to it.

decisions.choice: other people

decisions.choice: "người lân cận" (L, B); "người khác" (R) for neighbor

decisions.choice: "이웃" (L, B); "다른 사람들" (R)

decisions.choice: hangs: depends on, as a door hangs on its hinge
alternatives: is summed up and replaced by
decisions.reason: The two commands do not cancel the others. All the others rest on them.

decisions.choice: the law and the prophets: the Scriptures
decisions.reason: As in 5:17 and 7:12, where the golden rule is called "the law and the prophets".

decisions.choice: the law of Moses, the teachings of the prophets
decisions.reason: As in 5:17 and 7:12.

decisions.choice: la Loi ... les Prophètes, capitalised (L, B)

decisions.choice: "treo vào" (L); "dựa vào" (B), "dựa trên" (R) for "hangs"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of something hanging on a peg; Balanced and Readable say what it means, that the whole law depends on these two (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "달려 있다" for "hangs"
decisions.reason: Korean "달려 있다" keeps the picture of hanging and also means "depends on" (meaning decision).

es.R: Mientras los fariseos seguían juntos, Jesús les preguntó: \v 42 «¿Qué {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el que Dios prometió enviar?

decisions.choice: Psalm 110:1
decisions.reason: The psalm is headed "of David". It is the Old Testament verse the New Testament quotes most often of Jesus (26:64; Acts 2:34-35; Hebrews 1:13).

decisions.choice: the Lord ... my Lord: God, whose name stands in the Hebrew, and David's master
decisions.reason: In Psalm 110:1 the first "Lord" is God's name, which the Greek Old Testament gives as "Lord". "My Lord" is a different Hebrew word, used of a master or king. In Greek both are "Lord".

decisions.choice: at my right hand: the place of highest honor and shared rule
decisions.reason: The one seated at a king's right hand shared his authority (1 Kings 2:19).

decisions.choice: under, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: a footstool for, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet", the wording of the psalm in the Greek Old Testament. The SBLGNT reads "under your feet", as in Mark 12:36. The sense is the same: complete defeat of his enemies. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: spans on God's "my" and on "your" for David's Lord; none on David's "my"
decisions.reason: God speaks to the Messiah, so both their pronouns take the setting. "My Lord" is David's own word.

decisions.choice: the place of honor; defeat
alternatives: at my right; put under your feet
decisions.reason: Readable explains the right hand and what putting enemies under the feet means.

decisions.choice: Assieds-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} (L, R) with the setting; ‹ › for the psalm's words inside David's, inside Jesus's
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:36: French "s’asseoir" needs its reflexive pronoun, which the English "Sit" lacks, and it refers to the Messiah, so it carries the setting like "tes" in the same line. French marks the third level of quotation with ‹ ›: « » are Jesus's words and “ ” David's.

decisions.choice: upande wa kulia wangu
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of "at the right (hand)": the plain word for the right side, the place of honor (meaning decision m3). "Mkono wa kuume" is older and less familiar to many readers.

decisions.choice: God says "Ta" of himself and "{{deity_pronoun:con|Con}}" to David's Lord, both with the deity_pronoun span; "phán" for God speaking; "tôi" for David with no span
decisions.reason: As in Mark 12:36: Vietnamese must choose a word for "you" that states a relation, and "con" is how God speaks to the king he enthrones; it takes the span because the English "your/Your" does.

decisions.choice: "Chúa ... Chúa của tôi", with no divine-name setting; Readable adds "là Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: The Greek has kyrios twice, and the argument of 22:45 depends on David calling the Messiah "Lord"; Readable tells the two apart, as the English Readable does. Literal closes the question of 22:43 with "sao".

decisions.choice: "주님께서 내 주님께" (L, B); "주 하나님께서" (R); no divine_name span
decisions.reason: The Greek has kyrios twice; the wording of the Korean Mark 12:36. God speaks to David's Lord in 해라체, as God speaks in the Korean Old Testament (style guide, section 7a).

decisions.choice: tu: Senta-te, os teus inimigos
decisions.reason: God speaks to David's Lord, the Messiah, so the psalm takes "tu" (style section 4). The reflexive "te" of "Senta-te" is a pronoun for him and carries the setting with the possessives, as the English "your" does; Balanced says "Ocupa o teu lugar" for the English "Take your seat".

decisions.choice: O Senhor ... ao meu Senhor, with no divine_name span
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes the psalm in Greek, where both are "Lord", and the English has no divine_name span either; the meaning note says that the first stands for God's name.

decisions.choice: the verb of saying ("አለው") after God's words, which are set in ‘ ’ inside the psalm's “ ”
alternatives: "ጌታ ጌታዬን እንዲህ አለው፦" with the words after it
decisions.reason: Amharic usually closes a quotation with its verb of saying. The psalm is a quotation inside Jesus's words, and God's words a quotation inside the psalm, so they take a third kind of mark. Literal keeps the Greek order of the command and the time clause ("sit ... until"); Balanced and Readable put the time clause first, as Amharic prefers.

records.literal_gloss: If therefore David calls him Lord, how son of him is he?

en.L: If then David calls {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} Lord, how is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} his son?"
en.B: So if David calls {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} 'Lord', how can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be David's son?"
en.R: David calls {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} 'Lord.' So how can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be David's son?"

es.L: Si, pues, David {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llama Señor, ¿cómo es hijo suyo?».
es.B: Así que, si David {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llama “Señor”, ¿cómo puede ser hijo de David?».
es.R: David {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llama “Señor”. Entonces, ¿cómo puede ser hijo de David?».

fr.L: Si donc David {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}appelle Seigneur, comment est-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} son fils ? »

fr.R: David {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}appelle “Seigneur”. Alors comment peut-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} être le fils de David ? »

sw.L: Kama basi Daudi anamwita Bwana, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mwana wake jinsi gani?"
sw.B: Basi, kama Daudi anamwita 'Bwana,' {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anawezaje kuwa mwana wa Daudi?"
sw.R: Daudi anamwita 'Bwana.' Basi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anawezaje kuwa mwana wa Daudi?"

vi.L: Vậy nếu Đa-vít gọi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là Chúa, thì làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là con của ông ấy?"
vi.B: Vậy nếu Đa-vít gọi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là 'Chúa,' thì làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại là con của Đa-vít được?"
vi.R: Đa-vít gọi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là 'Chúa.' Vậy thì làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có thể là con cháu của Đa-vít được?"

ko.L: 그러니 다윗이 그분을 주님이라고 부르는데, 어떻게 그분이 그의 자손이냐?"
ko.B: 다윗이 그분을 '주님'이라고 부르는데, 그분이 어떻게 다윗의 자손이 되겠느냐?"
ko.R: 다윗이 그분을 '주님'이라고 부른다. 그런데 그분이 어떻게 다윗의 자손일 수 있겠느냐?"

pt.L: Se, então, Davi {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} chama de Senhor, como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é filho dele?"
pt.B: Então, se Davi {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} chama de 'Senhor', como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pode ser filho de Davi?"
pt.R: Davi {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} chama de 'Senhor'. Então como {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pode ser filho de Davi?"

decisions.choice: the Messiah is David's son and more: David's Lord
alternatives: the Messiah is not descended from David
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny that the Messiah descends from David (1:1; 21:9). He shows that the title says too little. Matthew has shown that he is the Son of God (3:17; 16:16).

decisions.choice: David's
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name David so that "his" is not taken to mean God.

records.literal_gloss: And no one was able to answer him a word, nor dared anyone from that day to question him any longer.

en.L: And no one was able to answer {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a word, nor did anyone dare from that day on to question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} any longer.
en.B: None of them could give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} any answer at all. And after that day no one was bold enough to put another question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: No one could answer Jesus at all. And from that day on, no one was brave enough to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} any more questions.

es.L: Y nadie podía contestarle ni una palabra, ni nadie se atrevió desde aquel día a interrogarlo ya más.
es.B: Ninguno de ellos pudo darle respuesta alguna. Y desde aquel día nadie se atrevió a hacerle más preguntas.
es.R: Nadie pudo responderle nada a Jesús. Y desde aquel día, nadie se animó a hacerle más preguntas.

fr.L: Et personne ne pouvait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondre un mot, et personne non plus n’osa, à partir de ce jour-là, {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interroger encore.
fr.B: Aucun d’eux ne put {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondre un seul mot. Et à partir de ce jour, personne n’eut plus l’audace de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} poser une question.
fr.R: Personne n’a rien pu répondre à Jésus. Et à partir de ce jour-là, personne n’a plus osé {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} poser de questions.

sw.L: Na hakuna aliyeweza kumjibu hata neno, wala hakuna aliyejasiri tangu siku hiyo kumhoji zaidi.
sw.B: Hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyeweza kumpa jibu lolote. Na tangu siku hiyo hakuna mtu aliyekuwa na ujasiri wa kumwuliza swali jingine.
sw.R: Hakuna mtu aliyeweza kumjibu Yesu chochote. Tena tangu siku hiyo, hakuna aliyethubutu kumwuliza maswali zaidi.

ko.L: 그리고 아무도 그분께 한마디도 대답할 수 없었고, 그날부터는 아무도 감히 그분께 더 묻지 못하였다.

ko.R: 아무도 예수께 대답하지 못했다. 그리고 그날부터는 아무도 예수께 더 질문할 용기를 내지 못했다.

pt.L: E ninguém podia responder-{{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} uma palavra, nem ousou alguém, desde aquele dia, interrogá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} mais.
